title: Saturation of a subset under a scheme groupoid is invariant
statement: Let $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ be a groupoid scheme [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. For every subset $A\subseteq|U|$, define $\sigma(A)=t(s^{-1}(A))\subseteq|U|$ using the underlying maps of points. Then $s^{-1}(\sigma(A))=t^{-1}(\sigma(A))$ as subsets of $|R|$. No openness, finiteness, flatness or separation assumption on the source and target morphisms is required.

source.place: Tag 03LO (lemma-constructing-invariant-opens), part (1), together with the subset-invariance equivalence following Tag 03BC (definition-invariant-open).

proof.text: Put $B=t(s^{-1}(A))$. Fix $r\in|R|$ with $s(r)\in B$, and choose $a\in|R|$ with $s(a)\in A$ and $t(a)=s(r)$. Let $P=R\times_{s,U,t}R$ with projections $p_0,p_1$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-base-change-image] with $f=s$, $g=t$ and $C=\{r\}$: $p_1(p_0^{-1}(\{r\}))=t^{-1}(s(\{r\}))$. The equality $t(a)=s(r)$ puts $a$ in the right hand side. Thus there is $z\in|P|$ with $p_0(z)=r$ and $p_1(z)=a$. This uses an image identity for scheme fibre products, without identifying their underlying spaces with topological fibre products.

source.place: Tag 03LO (lemma-constructing-invariant-opens), proof of (1), expanding Tags 022Q (lemma-pre-equivalence-equivalence-relation-points) and 0232 (lemma-groupoid-pre-equivalence).

proof.text: The groupoid laws in [def-a1-groupoid-scheme] give $s\circ c=s\circ p_1$ and $t\circ c=t\circ p_0$. Evaluating at the point $z$ from step 1 gives $s(c(z))=s(a)\in A$ and $t(c(z))=t(r)$. Hence $t(r)\in t(s^{-1}(A))=B$. We have proved $s^{-1}(B)\subseteq t^{-1}(B)$.

source.place: Tag 03LO (lemma-constructing-invariant-opens), proof of (1), expanding Tags 022Q (lemma-pre-equivalence-equivalence-relation-points) and 0232 (lemma-groupoid-pre-equivalence).

proof.text: For the reverse inclusion, take $r\in|R|$ with $t(r)\in B$. By the inverse laws $s\circ i=t$ and $t\circ i=s$ of [def-a1-groupoid-scheme], one has $s(i(r))=t(r)\in B$. The implication proved in steps 1 and 2, applied to $i(r)$, gives $t(i(r))\in B$, so $s(r)\in B$. Thus $t^{-1}(B)\subseteq s^{-1}(B)$, proving equality. The only input beyond set membership and groupoid identities was the scheme fibre-product image identity, so no openness, finiteness, flatness or separation hypothesis is used.
